items.title: shell App: deskSlothRemoteControl
items.box:
deskUnslothRemote: A SHELL APP ON ANDY'S NODE THAT RUNS deskUnsloth ON HIS PUPPET. Design 2026-10-10; capped to references, the specs live in the items.

VISION (Andy): a shell app that runs on both nodes at once, 11111 and 65432, reaching the same deskUnsloth on the puppet through the owner door and on its own node directly: one app, one code path, the target the only difference. "I am most interested right now in all the info that can be had from the unsloth server". Built step by step, one item at a time, in this goal without ever closing it, so verify does not run for an hour (goal/G14.3 holds the goal open).

ITEMS
- goal/G14.1 All changes required to make puppeteering work: the owner door's shim carries headers, so a command with a body runs on the puppet. Done, closed.
- goal/G14.2 A shell app skelleton with a connect/disconnect switch for Levant: deskUnsloth connect/state, the app with its target picker, the switch. Done, closed.
- goal/G14.3 Block the Goal/G14 from running the Verifier for an hour: his placeholder that keeps the goal open.
- goal/G14.4 The model selector dropdown line: the model line (cached models with capability icons, Load, the running mark, quant and GB), the known list as the answer with a cached flag, loads answered at once with their outcome, the chat box on both nodes. Done, closed.
- goal/G14.5 Build puppet-to-master Stream: on a puppet every server's published object goes to the owner, serialized, only while reachable; the master's shell hands it to onPublished with the sender; deskUnsloth keeps one state and publishes it; the Remote polls nothing. Done, closed.
- goal/G14.6 The First Tool: fetch data from the internet. Added 2026-10-10; its box is its spec.

LATER, at his word, one item at a time: VRAM and hardware, the studio's monitor and queue, the configuration view and editor, restart, a puppets list on the master, a filter at the source of the stream "if this proves to much", load progress during a load, and deskUnsloth serializing one studio operation at a time (the studio as a state machine).

chat.text: taking: gathering the tree facts a remote control of deskUnsloth needs, the owner door, the verbs a shell app can send a puppet, and where deskUnsloth keeps its two files. Your vision first; I write the box after it.

Facts in hand for the box, while you write the vision:
1. The owner door: owner.command on your loopback carries any node verb to a puppet and waits for its answer; today it fails for every verb that reads a body (the shim hands no headers), so that one-line fix in puppetMode is this goal first dependency.
2. deskUnsloth keeps its two files in its state folder on 11111, relay-state/process/deskUnsloth: configuration.json (persona, preamble, model, limits) and connection.json (url, key). fs.save through the node cannot write there, the write gate covers shell only; so the plain way is two verbs on deskUnsloth itself, read and write its configuration, reached from your shell through owner.command and jobs.api.
3. A restart after a change: jobs.cancel the deskUnsloth job on the puppet, then jobs.create with its script, both existing verbs; and what it does is readable the same way, jobs.get on its job, log and app object, by asking, since the puppet stream does not cross.
4. Your node keeps no puppet list; the app finds puppets by one owner.command per contact, or reads a list you keep.

Box written with your line at the top, the tree facts, and a shape marked proposed, not decided: a target picker, then the puppet deskUnsloth configuration shown and editable, a restart, and its job last lines as the monitor; every action an owner.command with an existing verb, and the one new thing two verbs on deskUnsloth itself to read and write its own files.
First item I propose, the dependency everything else rides on: the owner door shim hands the verb a request with headers. Add it?

I am most interested right now in all the info that can be had from the unsloth server, what can we get?

list of local models?

state of the VRAM cache?

all that stuff
does model selection affect available api's etc.

Plenty, and all of it read off the live server on this box just now. It is Unsloth UI Backend 2026.10.3 on 127.0.0.1:8888 with your key, and it publishes its whole api (openapi.json, 150 routes). What a remote control wants:
1. Models: GET v1/models lists every model it knows with quant, context length and loaded true or false (9 today, the Qwen loaded); GET api/models/local and api/models/cached-gguf add source, size in bytes and cache state; api/models/config/{name} the config; POST api/inference/load and unload switch the loaded model; api/inference/load-progress watches it.
2. VRAM and hardware: GET api/train/hardware: per GPU vram used and total (12.97 of 15.93 GB now), utilization, temperature, power draw and limit.
3. What it is doing: GET api/inference/status, the engine and context settings of the loaded model; api/inference/monitor, the monitor you see in the studio, with active model, queue (4 slots), and every api request with its prompt preview; api/inference/active-generations; api/models/kv-cache-estimate and api/inference/estimate-memory for the cache question.
4. Also there: chat threads and settings, training, audio, image; not ours.
The one implication: these live on the puppet box only, so the remote app gets them through deskUnsloth, a read verb or two on it that pass the studio answer through, each an owner.command and jobs.api away; no new node verb.

No for the api, yes for what it can do. The routes are the same whatever is loaded; the studio holds one model loaded at a time (status.loaded has one entry) and a chat request has to name that one. What changes with the model is reported by api/inference/status: supports_tools (true for the Qwen now), is_vision, is_audio, has_video_input (all false now), context_length (58880 for the Qwen, native 262144), parallel slots (4), offloaded layers (41). The Ollama models you saw are listed by the studio too, same route, loaded through it.
So the picker in the app shows each model with those flags and marks the loaded one; the endpoint never moves. One thing you may want to know: your deskUnsloth configuration says contextLimit 8192 while the loaded Qwen offers 58880.
the model that is running now is a quantized version of AgentWorld, does the unsloth server allow me to search for its remote models?

Not a free search of the hub: no route takes a search text for models. What it does give: for a repo you name, GET api/models/gguf-variants lists every quantization on Hugging Face with size, context length and whether it is downloaded; for your AgentWorld that is BF16 at 69 GB, UD-Q8_K_XL at 38 GB, down to the UD-Q2_K_XL you run at 24 GB. The hub source is huggingface (api/settings/hub). api/providers/model-catalog is the cloud providers list, OpenAI and the like, not the hub.
So the app can show the variants of any repo you type and start a download by loading one (gguf-download-progress watches it); finding new repos stays the studio or the hub page.
Does it list capabilities? vision, reason audio etc?

Partly. Per model without loading it: the task (text-generation, text-to-image, text-to-video), the format, the audio type, and two checks by name, api/models/check-vision and check-embedding, each a yes or no; the cached list adds has_vision. For the loaded model, status adds supports_tools, is_audio, has_video_input and the context length. Reasoning is not a flag anywhere for a local model; the cloud catalog carries reasoning and effort levels, the hub models do not.
So the picker can show task, vision, embedding and audio for every model, and tools, audio input and context for the loaded one; whether a model reasons you know from its name or by trying it.

items.title: All changes required to make puppeteering work
items.box:
WHAT: every change that makes puppeteering work, so that an owner command from Andy's node runs any loopback verb on his puppet and brings the answer back. Blocks every other item of goal/G14.

WHERE IT STANDS (read 2026-10-10, 84164a6b)
- Working: owner.command on his loopback signs a command for a puppet, the puppet's door checks it (puppetMode.ownerCommandIn), runs the verb through the loopback table (puppetMode.puppetDoor's shim) and answers on the command hash; his node hands that answer back in the same reply. Proven live 2026-10-10 from 65432 to 11111: the answer came on the hash.
- Broken: the shim gives the verb a request with no headers. Every verb reads its body through the one shared reader (serveCommon.readJsonBody), which begins with the content-length header, so it throws before parsing and the verb answers 400 bad-request, Invalid JSON body. Verbs taking no body get through; verbs taking one, which is nearly all of them, jobs.api included, do not. Reproduced here with the reader alone. No verb handler reads headers or the socket itself (checked: none in server.js); the reader is the only consumer.
- Already true of 11111: it is his puppet (owner.json names his key), it holds him as a contact, his node knows its key. Nothing else is needed on either node for the command to travel.

CHANGES
1. puppetMode.js, the shim: the request handed to the verb carries headers, content-type application/json and content-length of the body it holds. Still no socket, on purpose (G3: a handler that reaches for one fails alone). One place, a few lines.
2. The red, spirit/test/puppetCommands.js, written first: drives puppetMode.puppetDoor with the real codec and real keys, as puppetDoor.js does, but with handlers that read their body through the real serveCommon.readJsonBody; a command with a body is answered with what the body held, a command whose body is over BODY_MAX is refused by the reader as today's door refuses it, and a handler with no body still works. Red on today's code at the first check.
3. puppetDoor.js and ownerPost.js keep passing unchanged; their fake handlers never read a body, which is how this slipped past them, and the new suite is where that is held from now on.

THE PROOF, after the build: from his node, owner.command to 11111 with jobs.api and ask api answers the puppet's server trees; posted in this chat with the answer's first line.

NOT IN THIS ITEM: a verb to write owner.json on a node (the owner writes it by hand or by an installer, as face-install does); a puppet list on the owner's node; any deskUnsloth verb. Those are later items of this goal or none.

WHY: Andy, 2026-10-10: "First we fix the puppet-issue", "spit off one item for this: all changes required to make puppeteering work. you should be able to make that a green-able box in the first go. all other items will be blocked by it."

items.title: A shell app skelleton with a connect/disconnect switch for Levant
items.box:
WHAT: the hello-world of deskUnslothRemote, the brand new shell app: one switch that connects or disconnects Levant at the desk, with its state visible in the app. The app runs on both nodes at the same time: on 11111 it flips deskUnsloth on its own node; on 65432 it flips the same deskUnsloth on the puppet through the owner door. After goal/G14.1 (Andy: every other item is blocked by it).

WHY (Andy, 2026-10-10): "then one item for the hello-world state: I changed my mind on it's feature: it will be a connect/disconnect switch for Levant to be visible in desk." "this way i can turn it off, so i don't have to waive for you to claim both reds and code." And, correcting the box: "This will be visible in the brand new deskUnslothRemote shell-app, this is it's hello world and can simultaneously run un the puppet or on my own node."

HOW LEVANT IS AT THE DESK TODAY (read 2026-10-10): deskUnsloth loops every 250 ms asking its node's deskClient for the next lines, answers the lines addressed to its persona and JOB lines by posting through the desk, and nothing else; it declares no verb of its own. The desk counts an agent live for ten minutes after its last write (LIVE_MS), and every ask for lines is a write (the ear's listening word); the signoff verb takes an agent off the live list at once (goal/G8.5: "a leaving agent is not waited out for ten minutes"), and its next write makes it live again. The waive of a phase is decided by that live list.

SHAPE
1. deskUnsloth gains two verbs on its pipe: connect {on: true or false} answers {connected}, and state {} answers {connected, persona, model}. Disconnect: the loop stops asking for lines and deskUnsloth says signoff to the desk, so Levant leaves the live list at once, not in ten minutes, and the waive rule sees one agent. Connect: the loop resumes at the present, as it starts today (the backlog read, never answered), and its first ask makes it live again. The process stays up either way; stopping the job is not this switch. It starts connected, as today.
2. shell/deskUnslothRemote, the hello world: a target picker with two entries, this node and the puppet (the puppet's key from a small list in the app's own folder for now, until a puppets list exists), and the switch showing its state. On this node the app asks jobs.api with deskUnsloth state and connect; on the puppet it asks owner.command carrying that same jobs.api ask. One function with the target as its argument; nothing else differs. The same app opens on both nodes' shells at once, each with its own target.
3. Visible: the switch and Levant's connected state are shown in deskUnslothRemote itself, read from the state verb each time the app opens or flips; that the desk's live list follows is the effect, seen in its Team tab, not the display this item builds.

TESTS, the red first: a suite that starts deskUnsloth on a pipe against a fake node (as appFaceProcess.js does for the face) and asserts: state answers connected true at start; connect off stops the asks for next lines within a second, sends one signoff, and state says false; connect on resumes the asks; the app's one function builds the local ask and the owner.command ask from the same target. deskUnsloth's existing suite stays green.

FILES: process/js/deskUnsloth/deskUnsloth.js and its manifest; shell/deskUnslothRemote (new: the manifest, the page, the script); the new suite; no core file.

NOT IN THIS ITEM: the configuration view and editor, the studio's facts, the restart, the puppets list on the owner node. Each a later item of this goal.

items.title: Block the Goal/G14 from running the Verifier for an hour.
The model selector dropdown line.
items.box:
WHAT: two pieces of deskUnslothRemote for the chosen target (this node or the puppet). THE MODEL LINE under the switch: a dropdown of the models the studio has cached locally, each entry with its capability icons, the loaded one selected by default; a Load button when the chosen model is not loaded, the running mark when it is; the icons; small print with the flavor (quant) and the size in GB. THE CHAT BOX, sticky at the bottom edge of the panel, on the node that hosts deskUnsloth only: a title line with the model's info, a fixed-height scrolling display a quarter of the window high, an input line with a Send button; Enter sends; one line only.

RULINGS (Andy, 2026-10-10, capped; his words were in versions 1 to 11)
- The dropdown shows only models the studio has cached locally, the loaded one by default; each entry carries its capability icons "as far as you know it".
- Selecting loads nothing ("changing the selection only will bring more detailed info"); the Load button alone loads, shown for any model not loaded; the running mark in its place when loaded.
- ICON.VIEW for vision, THINK and MUSIC; "then show vision always".
- deskUnsloth "should cache the model list with all capabilities", so more is known of models not loaded; then "deskUnloth should REALLY cache the know list....": the known list IS the answer, at once, refreshed behind it.
- The chat box was shown only on the node that hosts deskUnsloth; lifted after goal/G14.5's stream: "so we should be able to run chat on 65432 just by removing the check", "stop! why, this should only be a change to the UI", "go." - the chat box is drawn for any target whose state answered, and the send goes through the chosen target.
- After the first build, live: the Load press died (the studio's load blocks); with no model loaded the selector did not show; the studio crashed; a failed load left the hourglass: "your UI must release the hour-glass status. and allow another loading attempt."; "deskUnloth must respond to all queries immediately, the remote need's to poll for status of a load, until it is known to have failed or succeeded."
- Q1 (does choosing load it): no. Q2 (does deskUnsloth chat with what Load loaded): closed on his "green? (after removing red Q)" with yes, his to overturn.

TODAY (read live 2026-10-10, Unsloth Studio 2026.10.3 at 127.0.0.1:8888 on the puppet box, bearer key from connection.json)
- GET api/models/cached-gguf: the cached list (13), repo_id, size_bytes, task, has_vision; 1 to 2 s. GET v1/models: every model known with quant and loaded, 15 to 18 s live (it probes its ollama entries). GET api/inference/status: of the loaded model, active_model, loaded, supports_reasoning, is_vision, is_audio; 0.3 s. Per-model routes (models/config, check-vision) are 2 to 4 s each and contradict cached-gguf on vision: not used.
- POST api/inference/load {model_path} BLOCKS until the model is in (minutes) and swaps the loaded one; GET api/inference/load-progress gives phase, bytes, fraction meanwhile; GET api/train/hardware gives VRAM used/total per GPU.
- All of it is loopback on the puppet box: only deskUnsloth can read it. A process answers jobs.api within DOOR_WAIT_MS, 12 s (appClient.js): nothing lengthy may be waited for in one ask.
- The icon table has no RUNNING: ON is the green circle, LOADING the hourglass.

SHAPE (built)
1. deskUnsloth models {} -> {active, cached, load, models: [{id, loaded, quant, bytes, task, vision, reasoning, audio}]}: THE KNOWN LIST, models.json in the state folder, answered at once, and a refresh from the studio running behind it (one at a time) so the next ask has what the studio said; only the first ask ever, with no file, waits for the studio. items.title: Build puppet-to-master Stream.
items.box:
WHAT: a stream from a puppet to its master: the master subscribes to one of the puppet's servers, and from then on every object that server publishes reaches the master's pages as it reaches the puppet's own, so the Remote polls nothing.

RULINGS (Andy, 2026-10-10)
- His sketch: "a puppet has a special, puppet command: stream (which starts a stream of posts to the master); the master that sends this to a puppet, then throws the streamed events into the node-broadcast for it's apps".
- "inside the puppet, the publisher then publishes to the master as well. Let's make sure this is the most simple thing possible."
- "publish-over-peer-post will be slow. so the master needs to select/filter at the source what he needs, he should be able to send a "subscribe to deskUnsloth", or a master stream should only contain appServer events."
- Then: "hmm, puppets are usually specialized, let's drop the specific app stream mechanism for now, and just send all app Server events. the other can be done later if this proves to much."
- And: "only while the master is live and reachable."
- And: "so deskUnsloth keeps a state, and publishes changes, it's own api are more like event-delivery to deskUnsloth"

CHECKED (2026-10-10, at ff2dfd3f)
- The publisher is one point in the node: appServer.publish calls jobs.report {app}; the node keeps the object on the job record (jobs.js, under the PAYLOAD_MAX gate) and emits job-updated, which server.js writes to every open page's event stream; the shell hands it to the app named after the process (deliverPublished, api.onPublished). Nothing of it crosses to another node.
- The puppet (11111) is a contact of the master, acquired as a relay member: its packets pass the master's front door and reach the page as packet events. A node posts with peer.post; the puppet's owner key is relay-state/owner.json.
- A puppet command is owner.command carrying a node verb through the owner door (puppetMode.puppetDoor runs the loopback handler). A new node verb needs his yes on the verb itself.
- The relay queues per target and refuses busy; a post per published object of one server is a handful a minute, a post per log line would not be.
- Publishers today: deskUnsloth (its state object, to be built with this item), desk and deskVerify (rules, runs), fileServer (transfer progress), chatClerver (every line). On the puppet: deskUnsloth and pushOrigin.

SHAPE (proposed on his rulings; no new verb)
1. NO SUBSCRIPTION: a puppet streams every server's published objects to its owner, always; nothing to switch on, no verb, nothing kept. Nothing else is streamed: no logs, no job states. A filter at the source is the later item "if this proves to much".
2. THE FORWARD, at the one point: where the node sets job.app and the node is a puppet (owner.json names another key), it also posts {module, app} to its owner as a packet named published, fire and forget (no wait, no retry), and ONLY WHILE THE MASTER IS LIVE AND REACHABLE: the same route check owner.command makes before a command (the route to the key, unreachable or without a relay means no post, no log line, nothing queued; the next change tries again). A post the relay refuses is one line in the node's log. Over PAYLOAD_MAX never reaches this point. SERIALIZED AT THE SOURCE (his question, 2026-10-10: "and the appServer publisings will be serialized at their source? they are peerposts after all."): one post to the owner in flight at a time; a module that publishes again while a post is out has only its newest object kept, posted when the one out returns (latest wins per module, order kept across modules), so a burst collapses and the relay never sees two posts from one puppet at once.
3. THE MASTER SIDE, at its one point: a packet named published from a contact is written to every open page stream as event published {from, module, app}, beside job-updated; the shell hands it to api.onPublished handlers of that module's app with the sender's key, so the Remote subscribes one way on both nodes and tells the puppet's object by `from`. Not from a stranger: the front door already drops those.
4. deskUnsloth KEEPS ONE STATE and publishes it on every change: {connected, persona, model, active, cached, load, models: [...], chat: {id, done, text}} (what state, models and chat.answer answer today). Its verbs are deliveries that change that state: connect {on}, model.load {id}, chat.send {lines}; each answers at once as today and the change arrives as the next published object. The read verbs state, models and chat.answer stay for a one-shot ask (a tool, a test), the Remote asks none of them: it draws from the published object, on either node, from the first one in.

items.title: The First Tool: fetch data from the internet.
items.box:
WHAT: Levant's first tool. deskUnsloth offers the model the tools the node describes to agents, the first being net.fetch, our proxy internet call; when the model calls one, deskUnsloth runs it through the node and hands the result back to the model, which answers with what it read. At the desk and in the chat box alike.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-10)
- The tools come from the node's uniform api introspection, nothing else; the conversion to OpenAI style is deskUnsloth's own ("we decided a while back that the conversion belongs to deskUnsloth").
- One object with two methods: convert the introspection to OpenAI tool descriptions; execute a tool when the model asks. The tool name maps to the verb call generically, no per-tool code.
- net.fetch is opened to agents with a verb file js/net/fetch.json, description "Fetch a page from the internet by url: GET unless method says otherwise; the owner proxy list decides which sites and which keys", and the net AGENTS.md line updated ("there is only key for very few fetches").
- Context length stays subject to experimentation until further notice. Then, seeing 1 % context use in the studio: "lets assume "auto" is most appropriate for now, and we'll get more nit-picky as we learn more": contextLimit "auto" in configuration.json means the studio's context_length of the loaded model (inference/status, read with every refresh of the known list), a number means that number; the prompt room and the tool room follow it.

CHECKED (2026-10-10, at 99118975)
- Introspection (goal/G10.5): ns.AGENTS is the namespace's AGENTS.md; ns.AGENTS.introspect lists the verbs that have a file js/<ns>/<verb>.json; ns.AGENTS.<verb> gives that file with request and reply filled in from the declaration as prototypes by example (net.fetch: url, method, headers, body, timeoutMs). The net folder has no verb file today, so introspect answers an empty list.
- The proxy: net.fetch is a loopback verb (wire), gated on every call by the owner's list relay-state/proxy.json; a key is filled in only for the hosts on that list; it relays the body whole. On 11111 there is no proxy.json: open, every host, no keys. Any process on the node may ask it through the loopback door.
- The model: inference/status says supports_tools for the loaded model; a live chat/completions with one tool answered finish_reason tool_calls with {name, arguments: {url}} in 2.2 s. OpenAI shape: tools [{type: function, function: {name, description, parameters}}], a tool name of letters, digits, underscore and dash; the answer's message.tool_calls; a message with role tool and tool_call_id carries the result; the model answers again.
- The studio refuses a request naming a model that is not loaded; deskUnsloth's model follows the load (goal/G14.4).
- The room: (contextLimit - answerTokens) * bytesPerToken, 8192 tokens on 11111 today; a page is HTML and large.

THE OBJECT, process/js/deskUnsloth/tools.js
- describe(namespace) -> OpenAI tools: asks ns.AGENTS.introspect, then ns.AGENTS.<verb> for each verb listed, and makes one tool each: name = the verb with its dot written as an underscore (net_fetch), description = the file's, parameters = a JSON Schema object with one property per request key, typed by its example (string, number, boolean, object). Nothing listed, no tools.
- run(call) -> the result as text, generic: the name read back to the verb (net_fetch is net.fetch), the node asked that verb with the model's arguments (only keys the request declares), for a verb describe listed and no other. The answer's body stripped of tags and whitespace and cut to TOOL_ROOM bytes (a quarter of the prompt room; the cut is said in the text). A refusal (the proxy closed by the owner, no such verb, a bad url) comes back as text in the node's words, so Levant says so instead of guessing.

THE LOOP, inside askModel: the tools from describe('net') go with every call; a tool_calls answer runs each call through run, appends each result as a tool message with its tool_call_id, and asks the model again; at most 3 rounds. When the rounds are spent and the model still asks for a tool, it is asked once more without tools and told the budget is spent, so its words are the answer (found live: three fetches of CodeMirror sources ended in a placeholder); only if that too says nothing does a placeholder stand. The published object's chat gains tool {name, url, done} while a tool runs, so the chat box can show it. Not a node verb, not a change to appServer.

TESTS, the red first: spirit/test/deskUnslothTools.js: the object alone first, against a fake node (net.AGENTS.introspect, net.AGENTS.fetch, net.fetch answering an HTML page, once a proxy refusal): describe gives the tool with the name, description and parameters typed from the examples, and none when the list is empty; run reads the name back to the verb, asks it with the model's arguments, hands the page back stripped and cut with the cut said, a refusal in the node's words, and refuses a name not listed. Then the process: the fake studio answers tool_calls then text; the call carries the tools; the loop runs the tool, asks again and posts the final text; three rounds at most; the published chat.tool while fetching. deskUnslothModels, deskUnslothSwitch and deskUnslothContext stay green.

FILES: spirit/run/js/net/fetch.json (new, core) and spirit/run/js/net/AGENTS.md (one line); process/js/deskUnsloth/tools.js (new), deskUnsloth.js and its manifest; spirit/test/deskUnslothTools.js (new); spirit/test/deskUnslothModels.js if the published shape grows.

LATER, not this item: other namespaces' tools; a tool on the Remote's side; keys for the puppet's proxy; a search engine; an MCP server over the loopback api (the same list and call, for any MCP client); contextLimit following the studio's context_length.

**My actual recommendation:**

- **Native OS text editing** → don't use Ace. Use a `textarea` or a native text widget. Ace is a web thing.
- **Web-based / browser OS (like SpiritOS might be if it's web-native)** → Ace is *fine*, but seriously consider **CodeMirror 6** — it's modular, ESM-native, and cleaner to integrate.
- **You specifically want Sublime keybindings + heavy multi-cursor editing** → Ace wins, as long as you can stomach the loading model.

So — is SpiritOS a **web-based OS** or a **native OS**? And what's the actual use case (config editor, file browser, REPL)? Tell me that and I'll tell you whether Ace is the right call or whether you're about to load a sledgehammer to crack a nut.

Want me to actually pull the Ace source (`ace.js`) and eyeball the bundle for you — see how fat it really is, whether it's got anything sketchy, what dependencies it drags in? That'd tell you the real integration cost.
you: wow. nah, i want colored one-person editing, or mostly just code viewing, since the coding here is mostly done by claude...
Levant: Okay, that changes everything, and it's a good change.

If **Claude does the actual coding**, then you're not the editor — you're the reviewer. You want something that *presents* Claude's output nicely and lets you eyeball/tweak if you feel like it. That's not an IDE. Ace is a sledgehammer you're now going to throw at a screen door.

Here's the real hierarchy for what you actually need:

**1. If it's mostly just *viewing* Claude's output** → you don't need an editor at all. **highlight.js** is 20KB, pure syntax coloring, zero editing machinery, zero dependencies. Drop it in, feed it a `<pre>` or `<code>`, done. This is literally all you need if Claude owns the writing.

**2. If you want *light editing* alongside viewing** → **CodeMirror 6**. This is the modern sweet spot: modular (you import only what you use — no fat bundle), ESM-native (no fighting the module system like Ace), great syntax highlighting, and it feels like a real editor when you actually want to fiddle with something. It does *not* feel like a full IDE, which is exactly right for your use case.

**3. If you want it to *look like VS Code*** → **Monaco Editor** (that's literally VS Code's editor). Beautiful, powerful, but heavy — probably overkill unless presentation polish matters more than bundle size to you.

**My actual pick for SpiritOS:** **CodeMirror 6.** It respects the "mostly viewing" reality while giving you the ability to actually touch the code when Claude's output needs a hand. It's the one that scales from "just a viewer" to "light editor" without pulling in an entire IDE.

The one thing I'd flag: whatever you choose, load it **ESM-only** in your OS build, not the legacy script-tag model. Anything that still uses `<script src="...">` is a smell you don't want in a modern OS.

Want me to pull CodeMirror 6's actual source and walk you through a concrete integration — how big it really is, what modules you'd actually need to import for colored viewing? That'd give you a real number on the cost rather than me guessing.
